paper.title_en: Fast Radio Bursts Trace Cosmic Star Formation with Little Delay
paper.abstract_en: The progenitor channels of fast radio bursts (FRBs) remain debated, with a central question being whether their cosmic rate traces star formation promptly or instead follows it with the long time-delay characteristic of compact-binary mergers. We perform a forward-modeling, hierarchical Bayesian analysis of the CHIME/FRB population, jointly fitting the catalog sample, baseband fluences, and localized host redshifts, while self-consistently incorporating the survey selection function through the injection framework. Adopting the classical cosmic star formation history (SFH) with a range of delay-time models, we find that the reconstructed FRB rate robustly tracks the SFH peak. All models exclude characteristic delays $Δt_d > 1.0$ Gyr at the 90\% credible level, with inferred median peak offsets in the range $Δt_d = 0.1$--$0.3$ Gyr that remain consistent with a prompt, zero-delay origin at the 2$σ$ level. This finding disfavors the previously reported multi-Gyr delays, strongly indicating that the central engine is linked to young remnants (likely magnetars) from stellar collapse and, potentially, to the prompt merger of compact objects.
